cards.text: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, is king of Judah, and his sovereignty and royal power are now established. Throne secure, kingdom steady, everybody can finally breathe.

cards.question: With Rehoboam's power established, what do he and all Israel with him do?

answers.text: They forsake the Law of the LORD
They rebuild the walls of Jerusalem
They make a treaty with Egypt

cards.text: Now it's the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign. Because they've been unfaithful to the LORD, a king comes to attack Jerusalem.

cards.question: In Rehoboam's fifth year, Shishak king of ___ attacks Jerusalem.

cards.text: Shishak brings 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen and countless troops out of Egypt: Libyans, Sukkites and Cushites. COUNTLESS, friend, that's when the guy with the clipboard just gives up.

cards.question: Shishak's army can't get past the fortified cities of Judah, so it never reaches Jerusalem.

cards.text: Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah are gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak. Then Shemaiah, a prophet, walks in with a word from the LORD, and I promise you nobody in that room is hoping for small talk.

cards.question: Shemaiah the prophet speaks to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah. What does the LORD say through him?

answers.text: You forsook Me so I forsook you to Shishak
Stand firm and I will drive Shishak out
Send gold and Shishak will turn back

cards.question: After hearing the LORD's word through Shemaiah, the king and the leaders of Israel ___ themselves.
When they hear the LORD's word, the king and the leaders say the LORD is being unfair to them.

cards.text: Instead, they say, "The LORD is righteous." And when the LORD sees that they have humbled themselves, His word comes to Shemaiah again.

cards.question: The king and the leaders have humbled themselves. What does the LORD tell Shemaiah He will do?

answers.text: He will make them rule Egypt

cards.text: He'll soon grant them deliverance, and His wrath won't be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak. But I KNEW there was a catch: Judah is still going to become Shishak's servants.

cards.question: Why does the LORD let Judah become Shishak's servants?

answers.text: To learn the difference between serving Him and serving other kings
To give Shishak enough gold to leave the land alone forever
To keep Egypt from attacking the northern tribes of Israel next

cards.text: So King Shishak of Egypt attacks Jerusalem and seizes the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He takes everything, even the gold shields Solomon had made.

cards.question: To replace Solomon's gold shields, King Rehoboam makes new shields out of ___.

cards.text: Rehoboam puts the new shields in the care of the captains of the guard at the palace entrance. Gold out, bronze in, like getting your nice watch swiped and wearing one from the gas station: hey, it still tells TIME.

cards.question: Whenever King Rehoboam goes into the house of the LORD, the guards carry the bronze shields with him and then return them to the guardroom.
Rehoboam humbled himself when Shemaiah brought the LORD's word. What happens to the LORD's anger toward him?

answers.text: It stays on all of Jerusalem

cards.question: The LORD doesn't destroy Rehoboam completely, and conditions in Judah are ___.

cards.text: So Rehoboam establishes himself and reigns in Jerusalem, the city the LORD chose to put His Name. He was forty-one when he became king and reigned seventeen years, and his mother was Naamah the Ammonite.

cards.question: Rehoboam does evil. What reason does the text give?

answers.text: He did not set his heart to seek the LORD
He trusted the gods of Egypt for protection
He listened to the priests of Jeroboam

cards.text: Everything Rehoboam did, first to last, is written in the records of Shemaiah the Prophet and Iddo the Seer. Somebody kept the receipts, friend.

cards.question: Rehoboam and Jeroboam, king of Israel, live at peace with each other all their days.

cards.text: Then Rehoboam rests with his fathers and is buried in the City of David. His reign is over, and the throne needs a new king.

cards.question: Which of Rehoboam's sons reigns in his place?

findings.problem: Card 3 says the king comes to attack Jerusalem, which gives away the answer to the true or false on card 6 (Shishak reaches Jerusalem). Card 6 also tests 12:4 only through a false statement. No story card ever tells that Shishak captured the fortified cities of Judah, so the baker can miss that detail.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He will make them rule Egypt' is silly. While Shishak is at the gates, no baker would believe it, so it doesn't sound like the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The story card has more than two beats. It covers Rehoboam establishing himself and reigning, the city the LORD chose for His Name, his age at accession, his seventeen-year reign, and his mother Naamah the Ammonite.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question 'What reason does the text give?' sounds like a test question. It doesn't sound like Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Rehoboam is 'son of Solomon,' and stop 2 card 10 calls Jeroboam 'king of Israel.' Neither fact is in 2 Chronicles 12. The cards cite only 12:1 and 12:15. The docs allow outside facts 'with their reference,' but the card's verses field is a single range inside the passage. So there is no way to cite an outside verse like 2 Chronicles 9:31 or 10:2.
findings.question: When a card states a helpful fact from outside the passage, such as who a person is, how should its reference be given in the JSON? Should the verses field be extended, should a separate field be added, or is the fact allowed without a reference when the person comes from earlier passages in the same story group?
